beats.narration: Fourteenth of March, 2024. A small town in Serbia. Three hundred and seventy people in the stands. And Olympiacos, three goals down.
By midnight, it was the biggest away win in the club’s whole European history.
Bill Shankly said football was more important than life and death. Ten thousand supporters in eighty countries voted it the greatest thing ever said about the game.

visual.text: I can assure you it is much, much more important than that.

beats.narration: In Piraeus, nobody needs that explained. They call this club Thrylos. The Legend.
But one week earlier, the Legend was dead and buried.
Round of sixteen, first leg. The Karaiskakis. 31,054 inside.
Six wins in a row since José Luis Mendilibar arrived in February. And Maccabi Tel Aviv? The last time, in 2010, they had knocked Olympiacos out on away goals. Unfinished business.
Mendilibar had been the manager for twenty-five days. A Thursday night in Piraeus, and the whole ground expected a win.
Nine minutes in, it was two-nil to Maccabi. Eran Zahavi. Ido Shahar.
El Kaabi pulled one back. Then Zahavi again. Then Dor Peretz.
One-three at half-time. A full Karaiskakis, and you could hear the Maccabi bench.
One-four. At home. The heaviest home defeat Olympiacos have ever suffered in this competition.
Mendilibar did not hide.

visual.text: This was a very bad game for us. They scored three goals on three chances and the result was justified.
visual.role: Olympiacos coach, after the first leg

beats.narration: On the other bench, Robbie Keane chose his words carefully. Remember them.

visual.text: All in all, we are just at halftime.
visual.role: Maccabi Tel Aviv coach, after the first leg

beats.narration: In Israel, the morning papers were a party.
Maccabi Tel Aviv jumps out to big lead over Olympiacos.

visual.headline: Maccabi Tel Aviv jumps out to big lead over Olympiacos, Haifa drops thriller

beats.narration: Three days later, it got worse. The derby. Panathinaikos, at the Karaiskakis.
Two home defeats in one week, one of them to the eternal enemy. If football is a religion, this was the week people stopped going to church.
The second leg was Maccabi’s home game, but it could not be played in Israel. Because of the war, it went to Serbia, behind closed doors, at the TSC Arena in Bačka Topola.
Three hundred and seventy people. And it was José Luis Mendilibar’s sixty-third birthday.

visual.label: In the ground in Bačka Topola

beats.narration: Maccabi had won their last five. They were ninety minutes from the first European quarter-final in their history. All they had to do was not lose by three.
Back in Piraeus, a whole city sat down in front of a screen.
Ten minutes. Daniel Podence. Four-two on aggregate.
Thirty-six. The captain, Kostas Fortounis. Four-three.
First-half stoppage time. Ayoub El Kaabi, with his head. Four-four.
Then Zahavi, from the penalty spot. Five-four Maccabi, again.
Sixty-five. El Kaabi again. Four-one on the night. The exact score of Piraeus, turned upside down.
Five each on aggregate after ninety minutes. Extra time.
Ninety-three. Stevan Jovetić, his first goal in European competition for fourteen years.
A hundred and three. Youssef El-Arabi, who had only come on in the eighty-eighth minute. Six-one.
Seven goals to five. From three down to the quarter-finals.
Robbie Keane, a week after halftime, had one line for the other dressing room.

visual.text: We did not expect such a defeat – congratulations to Olympiacos.
visual.role: Maccabi Tel Aviv coach, after the second leg

beats.narration: Proto Thema, in Athens, wrote that no team in European cup history had ever turned round a three-goal home defeat.
Conference League: Maccabi Tel Aviv, Olympiacos, one-six.

beats.narration: In Ireland, they wrote about the other side of it.

visual.headline: Robbie Keane's Maccabi Tel Aviv out of Europa Conference League after squandering three-goal lead against Olympiacos

beats.narration: Eran Zahavi had scored three of Maccabi’s five goals in the tie. He said it best.

visual.text: You can't concede six goals in Europe and continue on in this competition. Instead of making history, unfortunately we went the opposite direction.
visual.role: Maccabi Tel Aviv striker, after the second leg

beats.narration: And Mendilibar? He said they had never even talked about going through.

visual.text: But what we didn't talk about was qualifying.
visual.role: Olympiacos coach, after the second leg

beats.narration: Only about a good night. Then the second goal went in, and the third, and he said they were filled with confidence.

visual.text: We started with confidence and when the second and third goals came we were filled with confidence.
visual.role: Olympiacos coach, after the second leg

beats.narration: When the team landed in Athens, the supporters were there to meet them. Scenes of madness, the Spanish agency EFE called it.
Two months later, an English paper went looking for the great comebacks. Only three times in UEFA’s three competitions had a team lost at home by two goals or more and still gone through.
The Legend. A club with a laurel-crowned youth on its badge, and a week in March it will never let anyone forget.
Before the final in May, Mendilibar looked back at Bačka Topola. For sure, he said, that game showed everyone what we are capable of.

visual.text: For sure that game showed everyone what we are capable of.

beats.narration: Eleven weeks after that night, Olympiacos won the Conference League in Athens. The first European trophy ever won by a Greek club.
Piraeus. Bačka Topola. Athens.
Three hundred and seventy people saw it in the ground. Every Olympiacos supporter will tell you where they were when the sixth went in.
More important than life and death. Ask anyone in Piraeus about that week in March, and they will tell you Shankly was being modest.
end

description:
On 7 March 2024 Olympiacos lost 1–4 at home to Maccabi Tel Aviv in the Europa Conference League round of 16. Three days later they lost the derby to Panathinaikos. One week after the first leg, in an almost empty ground in Bačka Topola, Serbia — 370 people, on José Luis Mendilibar's 63rd birthday — they won 6–1 after extra time and went through 7–5. It is still the biggest away win in the club's European history, and eleven weeks later Olympiacos won the competition.

This film tells both nights from the stands: every goal, the words of Mendilibar, Robbie Keane and Eran Zahavi as they were printed, and what the papers wrote the morning after.

Every score, date and quote on screen is printed from FanLife's archive (UEFA match records) and the sources listed below.
